title: In, At and On: Basic Positions
summary: Choose in for a space or area, at for a specific location or point, and on for contact with a surface. Learn how different prepositions change the meaning when referring to the same object or place.
learningObjectives: Describe objects and people inside rooms, containers, towns and bodies of water using in.
Locate people at stops, entrances, windows, desks and road landmarks using at.
Describe objects on surfaces, pages, clothing and islands using on.
Distinguish in, at and on when a container, doorway or building can be viewed in more than one way.

explanation.heading: In: inside a space, area or volume
explanation.body: Use in when someone or something is inside an enclosed place, a larger area or a body of water. Typical expressions include in a drawer, in a kitchen, in a city, in the mountains and in a lake. In often answers the question “Inside what area or space?”
explanation.example: Several coins were hidden in a wooden box.

explanation.heading: At: a specific point or meeting place
explanation.body: Use at to identify a point or functional location rather than its interior. Common expressions include at the bus stop, at the entrance, at the door, at the traffic lights and at a desk. In directions, at often marks the point where you turn or stop.
explanation.example: A volunteer was waiting at the entrance to the hall.

explanation.heading: On: touching a surface or occupying an island
explanation.body: Use on when an object rests against a surface or is attached to one: on a shelf, on the ceiling, on a jacket, on the ground or on a page. People can also live on an island. On often answers “Which surface?” rather than “Which container?”
explanation.example: There is a handwritten note on the noticeboard.

explanation.heading: In versus on: the container and its surface
explanation.body: One object can be described from different perspectives. A letter in an envelope is inside it; an address on an envelope is written on its surface. Likewise, food can be in a bowl while a sticker is on the bowl. The correct choice depends on what is physically located where.
explanation.example: The biscuits are in the tin, and the price sticker is on the lid.

explanation.heading: At versus in: a point and an interior
explanation.body: A building can be treated as an interior space or as a point used to meet someone. “In the reception area” means inside that area; “at the main entrance” identifies the entrance as a point. Similarly, a person can wait at a door, while a sign hangs on the door.
explanation.example: Meet me at the library entrance; I will be in the reading room.

comparisons.title: Inside a container versus attached to it

left.label: In: interior
left.example: There is a spare key in the jar.
left.note: The key is enclosed by the jar.

right.label: On: surface
right.example: There is a paper label on the jar.
right.note: The label is attached to the outside surface.

comparisons.title: A person at a doorway versus a notice on it

left.label: At: location or point
left.example: A visitor is waiting at the door.
left.note: The visitor is positioned near the door.

right.label: On: surface
right.example: The opening hours are written on the door.
right.note: The writing is on the door itself.

comparisons.title: Inside a building versus at a landmark

left.label: In: inside
left.example: The children are in the sports centre.
left.note: The children are within the building.

right.label: At: a specific point
right.example: Their coach is at the sports centre entrance.
right.note: The entrance is identified as the meeting point.

examples.sentence: The puppy is sleeping in its basket.
examples.note: The basket surrounds the puppy, so in describes its position.

examples.sentence: Please wait at the tram stop opposite the museum.
examples.note: At identifies the stop as a specific place to wait.

examples.sentence: A colourful poster is hanging on the classroom wall.
examples.note: On shows that the poster is attached to the wall surface.

examples.sentence: There are three small villages in this valley.
examples.note: In describes a location within a larger geographical area.

examples.sentence: Someone left an empty cup on my desk.
examples.note: On indicates contact with the desk surface.

examples.sentence: The guests swam in the lake before lunch.
examples.note: People swimming within a body of water are in the lake.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The notebook is in the table.
commonMistakes.correct: The notebook is on the table.
commonMistakes.why: A notebook resting on a tabletop is on its surface, not inside the table.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The customer is waiting on the bus stop.
commonMistakes.correct: The customer is waiting at the bus stop.
commonMistakes.why: A transport stop treated as a point or meeting location normally takes at.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The sticker is in the outside of the lunchbox.
commonMistakes.correct: The sticker is on the outside of the lunchbox.
commonMistakes.why: A sticker attached to the outside is on that surface, not inside it.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The instructions are at page six.
commonMistakes.correct: The instructions are on page six.
commonMistakes.why: Written content located on a page normally takes on.

studyTips: For each item you see, ask whether it is inside a space, at a point or touching a surface; make one sentence for each relationship.
Sketch a container with one object inside and one mark outside; describe them using in and on.
Practise paired sentences with one landmark: a person at the door and a notice on the door.

exercises.prompt: The spare batteries are ___ the small drawer beneath the desk; open it to find them.
exercises.feedback: The batteries are inside the drawer, so in is the appropriate preposition.

exercises.prompt: Please wait ___ the main gate until a member of staff comes to meet you.
exercises.feedback: At identifies the main gate as a point where someone waits.

exercises.prompt: A map of the building is attached ___ the corridor wall.
exercises.feedback: A map attached to a wall is on its surface.

exercises.prompt: The guide said there are no permanent residents ___ the tiny island.
exercises.feedback: The usual expression for people residing on an island is on the island.

exercises.prompt: The visitor is waiting ___ . (the entrance; use in, at or on plus the given words)
acceptedAnswers: at the entrance
exercises.feedback: At the entrance locates the visitor at a specific point.

exercises.prompt: We found the missing bracelet ___ . (a jewellery box; the bracelet is inside it; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: in a jewellery box
exercises.feedback: In identifies the interior of the jewellery box.

exercises.prompt: The artist signed her name ___ . (the back of the painting; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: on the back of the painting
exercises.feedback: Writing located on a surface uses on.

exercises.prompt: My grandparents live ___ . (a small village; use in, at or on)
acceptedAnswers: in a small village
exercises.feedback: In describes location within a village.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: The event schedule is displayed at the wall beside the lift.
acceptedAnswers: The event schedule is displayed on the wall beside the lift.
exercises.feedback: A notice attached to a wall is on its surface, not at the wall.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: The children are swimming on the lake, surrounded by the water.
acceptedAnswers: The children are swimming in the lake, surrounded by the water.
exercises.feedback: Use in for people immersed in lake water; on would suggest a position on the surface.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: The directions are printed at page four of the leaflet.
acceptedAnswers: The directions are printed on page four of the leaflet.
exercises.feedback: Use on when specifying the page that contains printed information.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the location preposition in this sentence: A passenger is waiting on the bus stop opposite the hospital.
acceptedAnswers: A passenger is waiting at the bus stop opposite the hospital.
exercises.feedback: At indicates a stop used as a particular waiting point.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use these facts in one complete sentence: the passport / be / inside / the drawer. Begin with “The passport”.
acceptedAnswers: The passport is in the drawer.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use in to express the passport being inside the drawer.

speakingExercises.prompt: A colleague asks where to meet. Say one sentence beginning “Meet me” and use “at the main entrance”.
acceptedAnswers: Meet me at the main entrance.
speakingExercises.feedback: At identifies the entrance as a meeting point.

speakingExercises.prompt: Describe a notice attached to a door. Begin with “There is” or “There’s” and use the words “a notice on the door”.
acceptedAnswers: There is a notice on the door.
There's a notice on the door.
speakingExercises.feedback: On places the notice on the door surface.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the preposition and say the whole sentence: “The photo is in the wall.”
acceptedAnswers: The photo is on the wall.
speakingExercises.feedback: An image attached to a wall is on it, rather than inside it.

speakingExercises.prompt: Compare these two supplied facts in one sentence: the coins / be / in the jar; the price label / be / on the jar. Use “and”. Begin with “The coins”.
acceptedAnswers: The coins are in the jar, and the price label is on the jar.
speakingExercises.feedback: In marks the contents; on marks the outer surface.

speakingExercises.prompt: You want to tell a friend where your relatives live. Use the words “My relatives”, “live”, and “in a coastal town” in one sentence.
acceptedAnswers: My relatives live in a coastal town.
speakingExercises.feedback: In locates residents within a town.

speakingExercises.prompt: Produce exactly two sentences. First: a delivery worker / wait / at the gate. Second: a sign / hang / on the gate. Use the present continuous and begin with “A delivery worker” and “A sign”.
acceptedAnswers: A delivery worker is waiting at the gate. A sign is hanging on the gate.
speakingExercises.feedback: At identifies the meeting point; on describes the gate surface.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks where you put the clean plates. Reply in one complete sentence: “I put”, “the clean plates”, and “on the shelf”.
acceptedAnswers: I put the clean plates on the shelf.
speakingExercises.feedback: On identifies the surface supporting the plates.

listeningExercises.audioText: I left the tickets inside the blue suitcase, but the luggage tag is attached to the handle.
listeningExercises.feedback: Inside the suitcase means the tickets are in the luggage, not attached to its handle.

listeningExercises.audioText: The taxi will stop at the hotel entrance, so please wait outside rather than in the lobby.
listeningExercises.feedback: The requested meeting point is at the hotel entrance, not inside the lobby.

listeningExercises.audioText: A small silver bell was hanging on the front door when we arrived.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word location expression immediately after “hanging”.
acceptedAnswers: on the front door
listeningExercises.feedback: The bell hangs on the door surface, so the phrase begins with on.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children spotted several bright fish while they were swimming in the shallow river.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did the children see the fish?
listeningExercises.feedback: They were swimming in the river when they noticed the fish.

listeningExercises.audioText: The bus driver told us to get off at the next stop, just before the bridge.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did the driver ask passengers to leave the bus?
listeningExercises.feedback: The driver specified the next stop as the point for getting off.

listeningExercises.audioText: The picnic was on a small island, while everyone slept in cabins on the opposite shore.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did the picnic take place?
listeningExercises.feedback: The picnic location was the small island; the cabins were elsewhere.

listeningExercises.audioText: The receipt is in the brown envelope beside the keyboard.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word location phrase immediately after “is”.
acceptedAnswers: in the brown envelope
listeningExercises.feedback: In indicates the receipt is inside the specified envelope.

listeningExercises.audioText: You can read the full timetable on page twelve of the visitor guide.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression immediately after “timetable”.
acceptedAnswers: on page twelve
listeningExercises.feedback: Information printed on a particular page uses on.
